solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Hush punctures endlessly rude acting colleagues

indicators.note: without an end, so the final letter of the word for rude is dropped
to puncture something is to pierce into it, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: coarse, with its last letter removed
st! is an interjection calling for silence

explanation.surface: Someone shushing a crude actor in the middle of rehearsal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hush' looks like a command in the story but is just a two-letter interjection; 'acting colleagues' is the definition, not part of the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Co-stars are performers sharing billing in the same play or film, hence fellow actors.

clue.text: Costa Rican orchid that's neat? Yes, when from the south

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, as in neat's-foot oil

indicators.note: in a down entry, reading from the south means reading upwards, so the word for yes runs backwards

parts.note: ay is an old and dialect form of yes

explanation.surface: A tidy-looking flower from Costa Rica, apparently approved of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' looks like praise for the orchid but is the old word for oxen.
explanation.definitionFit: Cattleya is a genus of showy tropical American orchids, and one is the national flower of Costa Rica.

clue.text: Part of Samoa, hugely popular Pacific location

indicators.note: only a portion of the following words is wanted, a run of letters sitting inside them

parts.note: the letters straddle the two words

explanation.surface: Somewhere in Samoa is a hugely popular holiday spot in the Pacific.
explanation.walkthrough: Samoa is a real Pacific nation, so the surface keeps the geography plausible while the answer is actually in Hawaii.
explanation.definitionFit: Oahu is the Hawaiian island holding Honolulu and Waikiki, a heavily visited tourist destination in the Pacific.

clue.text: Feeling in Glasgow is cosmetic, sadly English unwanted

indicators.note: things that turn out sadly go wrong, so the letters end up in a different order
something unwanted is thrown out, so the letter for English is taken away

parts.note: taken as written
E is the standard abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A Glaswegian complaint that make-up is only skin-deep, minus any English.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the E from IS COSMETIC and rearrange the remaining nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Besides a Scottish idiom, Chambers gives Scoticism as Scottish sentiment or patriotic feeling, so it is a feeling found in Glasgow.

clue.text: Short dagger first-class? It's not permitted to have one

parts.note: A is a grade meaning first-class
NL abbreviates Latin non licet, it is not permitted
an ace is the one in a suit of cards

explanation.surface: Is this short knife top quality? You are not allowed to carry one.
explanation.walkthrough: NL for non licet is a dictionary abbreviation that only crossword regulars will know; the 'first-class' question is a red herring for ACE, which actually comes from 'one'.
explanation.definitionFit: An anlace is a medieval short two-edged dagger worn at the girdle.

clue.text: Leicester's boss is a mug

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the head of a sheep, the Leicester being a breed of sheep and boss slang for head
second meaning: a fool or simpleton

explanation.surface: A jibe that the manager of Leicester, the football club, is a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: Leicester reads as the city or its football club, but here it is a breed of long-wool sheep, and its boss is its head.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheepshead is an old word for a stupid person, a dolt, just as mug is slang for a gullible fool.

clue.text: Mostly, large fly did swarm in the Highlands

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter of the word for large is cut off

parts.note: big, without its final letter
a ked is a wingless parasitic fly, the sheep ked

explanation.surface: A large fly swarmed around in the Scottish Highlands, as midges do.
explanation.walkthrough: In Scots a bike is a nest or swarm of wild bees or wasps, and to bike is to swarm.
explanation.definitionFit: Biked is the Scots past tense of bike, a verb meaning to swarm like bees.

clue.text: Narrow-minded leader of opposition in the island

parts.note: borné, from French, means limited in outlook

indicators.note: the leader is whatever comes at the front, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: its opening letter

explanation.surface: A bigoted leader of the opposition in some island's parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: BORNE here is the French loanword borné, narrow-minded, not the past participle of bear.
explanation.definitionFit: Borneo is the large island in the Malay Archipelago shared by Malaysia, Indonesia and Brunei.

clue.text: Prize picker not fully set up? That's concerning

indicators.note: incomplete, so the final letter of the prize picker's name is missing
in a down entry, setting something up raises it so it reads from the bottom upwards

parts.note: ERNIE, the machine that draws British Premium Bond prizes, less its last letter

explanation.surface: A worry that the prize-draw machine has not been fully set up.
explanation.walkthrough: ERNIE is the random number generator that picks winning Premium Bonds, a British government savings scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: In re is the Latin phrase meaning in the matter of, used just like the preposition about or regarding.

clue.text: High tension surrounding one European language

indicators.note: to surround something is to enclose it, so one piece sits inside the other
someone high is intoxicated and muddled, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
a means one

explanation.surface: Heightened tension surrounding a single European country's language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High tension' reads as one electrical phrase, but High is the anagram signal and tension the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Estonian is the Finno-Ugric tongue spoken in Estonia, a European Union member on the Baltic.

clue.text: Leaving Centre, walked in water northwards with early freshness forgotten

indicators.note: leaving means departing, and the centre is the middle letter that departs
in a down entry, going north means travelling up the column, from the bottom letter to the top

parts.note: waded, its middle letter removed

explanation.surface: Someone paddling north through water in the morning, no longer fresh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forgotten' marks the answer as an obsolete word; deaw is Spenser's spelling of dew.
explanation.definitionFit: Dew is the moisture of early morning, the emblem of freshness, and deaw is its archaic Spenserian form.

clue.text: Treat with quinine? Something easy is occupying one

parts.note: a cinch is a very easy task

indicators.note: something occupying a space sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A query whether quinine treatment is simple once it is in somebody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Occupying one' is read literally: the short word goes inside the word one, not inside a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Quinine comes from cinchona bark, and to cinchonise is to dose someone with quinine or cinchona.

clue.text: In Edinburgh that skimpy swimwear's no good

indicators.note: no good means without good, so the letter standing for good is struck out

parts.note: a thong is a minimal bikini bottom
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A Scottish verdict that some revealing swimwear is unacceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: Thon is a Scots demonstrative meaning that or yon, used of something at a distance.

clue.text: One old test not depicting rural life

parts.note: 'un is the dialect form of one, as in a good 'un
past means former, old
an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: A single dated exam that has nothing to do with the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastoral art or writing portrays country life, so its negation describes work lacking any such rustic subject.

clue.text: Drop of alcohol and seaman's on about bloomers

indicators.note: turned about means facing the other way, so the whole string is read backwards
a drop is a tiny amount, so only the first letter of the drink is used

parts.note: its first letter
a tar is a sailor
re means on or concerning

explanation.surface: A tipsy sailor rambling on about ladies' knickers.
explanation.walkthrough: Bloomers looks like underwear, but here it means blunders, mistakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Errata are listed errors in print, and a bloomer is a blunder, so the plural noun matches mistakes.

clue.text: Malaysian lord keeping time oddly for piece worker

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it within, so the title encloses the selected letters

parts.note: tuan is the Malay title meaning sir or lord

indicators.note: odd positions, the first, third and so on, supply the letters

parts.note: first and third letters

explanation.surface: A Malaysian nobleman irregularly holding on to time while hiring a casual labourer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutman is a dialect term for a labourer paid by the piece rather than by the hour.

clue.text: Pottery teacher potting nothing paltry

indicators.note: to pot something is to put it inside a vessel, so these letters go within the teacher

parts.note: a barbe was a Waldensian preacher and teacher
O looks like zero
tin as in tin god or tinpot, meaning cheap and paltry

explanation.surface: A pottery class where the teacher pots nothing worth having.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potting' suits the pottery surface but is the instruction to put pieces inside. The teacher is a Waldensian preacher, a Chambers-only sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbotine is clay slip used to decorate ceramics, and by extension pottery decorated in relief with it.

clue.text: Flautist periodically allowed in Scotland

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so every second letter is taken

parts.note: second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: A flute player is only sometimes permitted to perform in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Luit is a Scots past tense of let, so it means permitted.

clue.text: University boy with a first from LSE sounding together

parts.note: uni is the short form
a son is a boy
taken as written

indicators.note: the first means the opening letter, taken from the following word

parts.note: its first letter

explanation.surface: A university student who earned a first-class degree at the London School of Economics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First' suggests a top degree; here it just takes the opening letter of LSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Unisonal describes voices or instruments in unison, producing the same pitch at once.

clue.text: Write in English for George Town

parts.note: to pen is to write
Ang. abbreviates Latin Anglice, in English

explanation.surface: An instruction to write the name of George Town in English.
explanation.walkthrough: Anglice is the Latin adverb used in dictionaries to mean in English.
explanation.definitionFit: George Town is the capital of the Malaysian state of Penang, and the city itself is commonly called Penang.

clue.text: Present Queen holds a view that's disguised

indicators.note: to hold something is to have it inside, so the slang word encloses the rearranged letters

parts.note: queen is slang for a gay man

indicators.note: a disguise changes how something looks, so its letters appear in another order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A monarch holding back her true opinion about a gift.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen points at royalty, but here it is the slang term.
explanation.definitionFit: A giveaway is a free gift, something handed over as a present.

clue.text: Taking advantage, furious Head canes on occasion, as before

indicators.note: a furious person is in a wild state, so the letters are thrown into disorder
taking something away removes it, so those letters come out of the fodder

parts.note: ad is short for advantage in tennis scoring
taken as written

explanation.surface: An enraged headteacher seizes the chance to beat pupils now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As before' marks an obsolete word, here a Spenserian one.
explanation.definitionFit: Encheason is an archaic word for a reason or cause, the occasion for something happening.

clue.text: Television screening one old ruler and bishop on a fasting day

indicators.note: to screen something is to show it within a frame, so the following pieces sit inside

parts.note: TV is the abbreviation
Roman numeral one
the shah was the former monarch of Iran
B is the chess notation for bishop
taken as written

explanation.surface: A TV broadcast showing a former monarch and a bishop on a religious day of fasting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screening' fits the television picture, but it means the two letters of the abbreviation enclose everything else.
explanation.definitionFit: Tishah b'Av, the ninth of Av, is the Jewish fast mourning the destruction of the Temples in Jerusalem.

clue.text: Indians echo line

parts.note: the Incas were the native people of Peru
Echo is E in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A row of Native Americans, or one echoing a line of speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Incase is a variant of encase, to enclose or cover, as one lines a box with a covering.

clue.text: Apprentice publicity causing damage no longer

parts.note: app is short for apprentice
to give something an airing or air is to publicise it

explanation.surface: A trainee's media exposure doing harm to their career.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No longer' marks an obsolete word.
explanation.definitionFit: Appair is an obsolete form of impair, meaning to harm or weaken.

clue.text: Agree rise on the radio

indicators.note: radio is heard, not seen, so a word with the same sound but other spelling is needed

parts.note: an ascent is a rise or climb

explanation.surface: A broadcaster agreeing to an increase announced over the airwaves.
explanation.definitionFit: To assent is to consent or say yes, a formal synonym of agree.

clue.text: Old enemies are fine with joke

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
one as in 'have you heard the one about...', a joke

explanation.surface: Former foes who are relaxed enough to share a joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old' marks an obsolete plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Fone is an obsolete plural of foe, so it means enemies in archaic English.

clue.text: Foul-smelling resin in fact not opened

indicators.note: with no opening, so the initial letter is missing

parts.note: a thing is a fact, as in 'the thing is...'

explanation.surface: A smelly resin that, in fact, has never been unsealed.
explanation.definitionFit: Hing is another name for asafoetida, a gum resin with a strong sulphurous odour used in Indian cooking.

clue.text: Nick's to start to move

definitions.meaning: second meaning: to begin moving after rest

explanation.surface: Someone named Nick is about to get going.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick looks like a man's name; it is British slang for jail, as stir is.
explanation.definitionFit: Stir is slang for prison, and to stir is to begin to move, as a sleeper does on waking.

clue.text: Henry in battered Panama hat getting evidence of complaint

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the king's letter sits within the other letters
something battered is knocked out of shape, so its letters are reshaped

parts.note: PA is the international code for Panama
taken as written
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Henry sporting a beaten-up straw hat that hints at some illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Panama hat' reads as one item; only PA is drawn from Panama.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphtha is a small mouth ulcer, as in thrush, so it is a visible sign of an ailment.

clue.text: Turned up once topless? That's cut!

indicators.note: without a top, and in a down entry the top is the first letter, so it goes

parts.note: shewn is an archaic spelling of shown, and to show is to turn up

explanation.surface: Someone appeared topless one time, and a director shouts to stop filming.
explanation.definitionFit: Hewn is the past participle of hew, to chop with an axe, so it means cut.

clue.text: Strain to develop form of insect

indicators.note: developing means changing form, so the letters take a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A strain of insect that is beginning to develop.
explanation.definitionFit: An instar is an insect's stage between two moults, one of the forms it takes while growing.

clue.text: Sight that is seen in Polo?

indicators.note: something seen in a car is inside it, so these letters sit within the other piece

parts.note: the Polo is a Volkswagen car
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: A question whether this is the vista one sees in a game of polo.
explanation.walkthrough: Polo suggests the horseback sport or the mint; it is the Volkswagen model, so stands for VW.
explanation.definitionFit: A view is what can be seen from a place, a sight or prospect.

clue.text: Cuckoos in the country for artificial reduction

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the birds sit within the land

parts.note: a nation is a country
the ani is a black tropical American cuckoo

explanation.surface: Mad people across the land campaigning for artificial cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: Cuckoos looks like slang for crazy people; it is the birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Nanisation is the deliberate dwarfing of plants, as in bonsai, an artificial reduction in size.

clue.text: Term for excessive luminance involved with 60% of argon

definitions.text: Term for excessive luminance involved with 60% of argon

indicators.note: something involved is tangled up, so the letters get mixed
a term is an end point, so the closing letter of the next word is taken
sixty percent of a five-letter word is its first three letters

parts.note: its last letter
L is the physics symbol for luminance
first three of its five letters

explanation.surface: A technical definition of dazzle in a gas-filled lamp, given partly in argon.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: glare is the word for excessive brightness, and the letters E, L and ARG are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Glare is the dazzling discomfort caused by excessive brightness, the term lighting engineers use for too much luminance.

clue.text: Criminal activity surprisingly clear and near once

indicators.note: a surprising outcome is unexpected, so the letters come out in an unexpected order

parts.note: taken as written
ny is an obsolete word for near, nigh

explanation.surface: A crime that was unexpectedly obvious and close at hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Larceny is the legal term for theft, a form of criminal activity.
